svg.title: Template Method
svg.desc: Template Method. Fix an algorithm's skeleton in a base class and let subclasses fill in individual steps, without changing their order. Step 1, Copy-paste importers: Each importer copies the whole import: the name-check fix reached CsvImporter, not JsonImporter. Step 2, The skeleton in the base: run() lives once in DataImporter and calls the steps in order; subclasses fill in parse() only. Step 3, One run, step by step: run('products.csv'): parse runs in CsvImporter, the default hook rejects 1003: 4 saved, 1 rejected. Step 4, Hooks, and the alternative: JsonImporter overrides the hook to also require a positive price; DataImporter stays untouched.

g.text: Each importer copies the whole import: the name-check fix reached CsvImporter, not JsonImporter.
run() lives once in DataImporter and calls the steps in order; subclasses fill in parse() only.
run('products.csv'): parse runs in CsvImporter, the default hook rejects 1003: 4 saved, 1 rejected.
JsonImporter overrides the hook to also require a positive price; DataImporter stays untouched.
Hollywood principle: don't call us, we'll call you
The base class calls the subclass's parse(), never the other way round
this.parse(row) runs CsvImporter's code: this importer is a CsvImporter
CsvImporter doesn't override validate(), so the hook's default runs
Added without editing DataImporter or CsvImporter
Only parsing really differs, yet both classes copy all six steps: the fix reached one copy
has a default, may be overridden
Java AbstractList: implement get() and size(), inherit the rest
Python unittest.TestCase: run() calls setUp(), the test, tearDown()
Spring JdbcTemplate: the same idea by composition, with callbacks
Cost: each variant is a subclass, coupled to the base class
vs Strategy: compose the whole algorithm and swap it at runtime
Relatives: a step is often a factory method; at scale, pipes and filters
